Academic claim restricted to the specified 60+35=95 EC compulsory core; 25 restricted and 30 final-work EC unassessed, genuine 30 open separate. No outgoing IRO/POL/IP conditions borrowed.

interestReview.finding: All current rows reconciled and subject matter independently corroborated; source Excel IDs and physical registry rows distinguished. No registry/role change. Canonical concepts use current official NIP evidence directly.

academicJudgment.claimTested: Two complete feasible UCR programmes meaningfully respond to the confirmed 95 EC NIP compulsory core through sustained political theory, comparative/international/EU politics, policy, qualitative and quantitative methods and concrete psychological and institutional study. The second gives substantially more weight to democratic publics and communication. Dutch political and political-psychology depth remain different. This is not a comparison of the restricted specialization, final research, full degree or graduation eligibility.
academicJudgment.strongestObjection: A 95 EC core excludes advanced specialization and final research; UCR cannot reproduce the Dutch political system sequence or all political psychology. A communication emphasis must not be generated solely from an optional media title or substitute generic persuasion for political science. The published 180 EC sum alone proves neither eligibility nor academic equivalence.
academicJudgment.finding: The restricted claim is supported by a specified, substantial compulsory academic object: national/comparative/international/EU politics, theory, philosophy, economics, qualitative/quantitative inquiry, psychology and research design. Both UCR plans retain all six politics courses, substantive quantitative and qualitative research and meaningful social/psychological study. The second adds actual rhetoric, framing/persuasion, ideological language, representation and bargaining inquiry while retaining the political foundations. Dutch politics and complete political-psychology depth remain explicitly different. The limited comparison does not depend on the uninstantiated advanced choices, 10 EC seminar or 20 EC thesis.
academicJudgment.adverseTest: A future package heavily weighted to Dutch policy, security, communication, political behaviour or intensive specialized thesis methods could reverse a whole-degree claim. All 55 EC of restricted/final study are therefore unassessed, not declared immaterial. The independently specified 95 EC core and the genuine uninstantiated 30 EC open category survive without invented module membership or waivers.

uncertaintyTests.fact: Applicable later NIP course eligibility/offerings, five-of-ten restricted-choice combinations and seminar/thesis entry and assessment remain unverified.

courseReview.finding: Read actual current workbook evidence and per-course contributions. Two complete programmes: nine and nine advanced courses respectively; full offerings/prerequisite and numerical checks must pass. No absent outline material, invented political dataset or guaranteed specialist supervision.

alternativesAndStopping.finding: Two concepts were specified before selection. Both actual schedules pass 24 unique courses, 180 EC, six terms, Year-1 PPD and advanced requirements. They differ by seven courses/52.5 EC each way for substantive institutional-economic versus democratic-public communication priorities. A dedicated climate third candidate is not supported as a stable selected direction in the assessed core; stop without a third. All 32 inherited registry rows retain compiler exclusion; concepts are independently based on exact NIP official sources.

alignmentReview.finding: Dutch Politics and the broad theories/approaches component remain separate blanks; no generic title-based replacement. Political-psychology correspondence is only to actual social influence, attitudes, group and prejudice content. Public Economics addresses an identifiable economic/public-choice part, not full rational-choice equivalence. Data Science aligns to an important actual R/data-analysis function, complemented by the separate real statistics and econometrics sequence. Neither design/report functions nor hypothetical projects force remaining research rows. All excluded choices/open/final work remain unmatched. Optional research stays outside each 180 EC and is placed with PPD because final-work comparison is withheld.

readerValues.programmeDescription: Leiden’s National and International Politics route studies power, institutions and public policy in the Netherlands, Europe and the wider world. It develops comparative, qualitative and quantitative research skills and ends with a supervised individual thesis.
readerValues.comparisonExplanation: This comparison assesses Leiden’s confirmed 95 EC compulsory political-science core. UCR can combine sustained comparative and international politics with policy, political theory and empirical research, or give more weight to political behaviour and public communication. Dutch political specialization and the complete political-psychology sequence differ. The 25 EC restricted choices, 30 EC seminar and thesis, and full degree progression are excluded from the claim; 30 EC of genuine open study is shown separately.

curriculum.limitation: The published structure totals 180 EC. Only the 95 EC compulsory core is academically assessed here. The 25 EC restricted choices and the 30 EC seminar and thesis are retained as published categories but remain unassessed; detailed eligibility, offerings and final-work rules are unverified. The separate 30 EC open space has no assumed contents. A complete valid entrant pathway is not certified.

componentNotes.nip1-01: Studies Dutch elections, parties, coalition formation and relations between government and parliament.
componentNotes.nip1-03: Introduces political science approaches, including institutionalism, constructivism, feminism, Marxism, political psychology and normative theory.
componentNotes.nip1-06: Studies the democratic rule of law in the Netherlands, with comparisons to neighbouring countries and the United States.
componentNotes.nip1-09: Introduces statistical description, testing and data analysis using R.
componentNotes.y2-01: Builds on introductory statistics and develops multivariate analysis using political data and R.
componentNotes.y2-04: Connects economic models and rational choice to political behaviour and policy, including growth, inequality, trade and climate.
componentNotes.y2-05: Studies how emotions, prejudice, personality and group dynamics influence political behaviour.
componentNotes.y2-06: Forms part of the second-year research training: students analyse evidence and communicate findings in writing and presentations.
componentNotes.y2-07: Students develop their own political research proposal and practise giving constructive feedback.
componentNotes.y2-08: Choose five different 5 EC courses from: Democracy and Autocracy; States, Trade and Development; War, Peace and Security; Migration and Borders; Environment: Politics and Policy; Media and Political Communication; Politics of International Law; Philosophy of Freedom and Equality; Polarisation and Populism; The Netherlands in the World. The detailed course eligibility and offering rules for this route still need confirmation. This component is displayed as published but is outside this comparison’s assessed compulsory core.
componentNotes.y3-01: Thirty EC may be used for electives, a minor, study abroad or an internship. Selected courses require approval, with an exception for recognised 30 EC Leiden, Delft and Erasmus minors; sufficient level and no overlap with compulsory study are required. Honours courses and the Political Science, Mini-minor Political Science and Introduction Social Sciences minors cannot fill this space. Places and individual eligibility are not guaranteed.
componentNotes.y3-02: A specialist seminar uses current literature, discussion and research-led learning. Topics such as populism, security, climate policy and digital democracy are examples. Entry and assessment rules for this route still need confirmation. This component is displayed as published but is outside this comparison’s assessed compulsory core.
componentNotes.y3-03: Students formulate a question, design and conduct their own political science research, and write an individual thesis under supervision. A supervision plan is agreed with the first reader. Entry and assessment rules for this route still need confirmation. This component is displayed as published but is outside this comparison’s assessed compulsory core.
